question: How many milliseconds does each steady-yellow and steady-red stage last in Figure 4J-3?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Figure 4J-3 does not assign any durations (in milliseconds or otherwise) to its stages — it illustrates only the sequence of indications for a pedestrian hybrid beacon, not their timing. The only timing information in the evidence is Guidance that the steady yellow change interval should last 3 to 6 seconds (i.e., 3,000–6,000 ms); the duration of the steady red stage corresponds to the pedestrian walk interval and is not given a fixed value in the evidence provided. Standards (mandatory): - "Following an actuation by a pedestrian, a pedestrian hybrid beacon face shall display a flashing CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by a steady CIRCULAR yellow signal indication, followed by both steady CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian walk interval, followed by alternating flashing CIRCULAR RED signal indications during the pedestrian change interval (see Figure 4J-3)." No specific durations are mandated. Guidance (recommended): - "A steady yellow change interval should have a minimum duration of 3 seconds and a maximum duration of 6 seconds (see Section 4F.17). The longer intervals should be reserved for use on approaches with higher speeds." (equivalent to 3,000–6,000 milliseconds) Options (permitted): - "A steady red clearance interval may be used after the steady yellow change interval." (No duration is specified for this optional interval.) Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 4J-3 shows the six-stage sequence (dark, flashing yellow, steady yellow, steady red during walk interval, alternating flashing red during change interval, dark again) with no time values attached to any stage; [Image 4] page 730 contains the operational Standard describing the sequence but no millisecond timing. Citations: - Section 4J.03 Standard §2 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Guidance §11 (p.730) - Section 4J.03 Option §12 (p.730) - Figure 4J-3 (p.729) - Page 730
